- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.2), model reacts too slowly; adjust forecast to match sentiment shift within 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ price + sentiment-weighted trend.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.4–0.6) and price is flat, model often predicts minor drift; forecast should be within ±1% of recent 7-day average.
